To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the first structure of a photosynthetic bacterioferritins shows the heme molecule located in a crystallographically special position.
the structure of Rhodospirillum rubrum bacterioferritins has been determined and that the structure of R. capsulatus bacteriopurpurin has also been determined.

the structure of the first bacterioferrin from a photosynthesizing organism has been determined at 2.60 A resolution and that the structure shows that the heme is bound in two orientations, thus satisfying crystallographic and molecular symmetry.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a bacteriof ferritin from a photosynthesis-competent organism and shows that the protein structure of this ferritin is similar to the one of the E. coli protein.
the structural characterization of heme-containing proteins and the elucidation of their biological function.
the elucidation of the structure and the mechanism of the heme binding and the oxidation of Fe(II) to Fe(III).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Rhodobacter enzyme is in a metal-free state, but with the possibility of a metal ion being bound to the site in a fraction of the subunits.
the heme molecule is bound in the hydrophobic pocket in a noncrystallografic site, whereas the ferroxidase site is empty or fractionnaly occupied.
the heme molecule in the Rhodobacter bacterioferritins has a different orientation than in E. coli.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the heme molecule is located in a hydrophobically shielded cavity of the bacterioferritins.
the Rhodobacter ferritin is a very similar structure to the Escherichia ferritins, and that the heme molecule is situated on a special position in the crystal lattice.
the structure of Rhod. caps. bacterioferrin has been solved at 2A resolution, which reveals the first structure of a heme bound to a bacterioferring.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the bacterioferritins from photosynthetic organisms are not significantly different from their nonphotosynthetic counterparts.
the heme molecule is not a cofactor of the ferroxidase activity but a structural element that is necessary for the stability of the protein.
